rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whom believers may fight are people characterized by fighting them, excluding those who do not fight, such as children.
rows.anchor: وقال { الذين يقاتلونكم } أي من شأنهم قتالكم لا من ليس شأنه ذلك كالصبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording suggests that fighting is permitted in response to their fighting, as its cause, rather than at a particular time; the imperfect fixes no time.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشعار بأن القتال عن سبب المقاتلة فهو مما يفعل عن سبب لا مما يفعل لوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb indicates occurrence of the act without fixing it to a particular time.
rows.anchor: وصيغة المضارع لم يقصد بها إلا صدور الفعل من غير نظر إلى زمان مخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God commands justice even toward enemies, the ban bars initiating combat against protected people, treachery, killing women and children, and killing old people who pose no threat.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الله سبحانه وتعالى قد أوجب العدل في كل شيء حتى في حق أعدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition also bars continuing to fight after an enemy offers peace; the omitted object broadens its scope, and the derived form signals deliberate transgression.
rows.anchor: ودوام القتال لمن ألقى السلم بعد الابتداء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of the prohibition expands its scope, and the derived verb form signals intentional wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: فحذف المتعلق اختصارا فأفاد زيادة المعنى وهو من غريب أفانين البلاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not treat transgressors with the kindness shown to one whom He loves; this applies to transgression generally, here and elsewhere.
rows.anchor: مطلقا في هذا وغيره , أي لا يفعل بهم من الخير فعل المحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forbidding transgression, the passage explicitly permits fighting those who fight the believers.
rows.anchor: ولما حرم الاعتداء صرح بإباحة أصل القتال

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Thaqifa can mean solidity or skill and alertness; thaqiftu can mean finding or seizing something.
rows.anchor: لأنه من ثقف بالضم ثقافة إذا صلب وثقف أي بالكسر كذلك

rows.speaker: ابن القطاع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qattaʿ explains thaqiftu as taking hold of a thing or encountering it.
rows.anchor: ثقفت الشيء ثقفا إذا أخذته والشيء صادفته - قاله ابن القطاع . وقال الأصبهاني

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani defines finding someone as encountering him in a way that enables capture or defeat.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصبهاني : والثقف وجوده على وجه الأخذ والغلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified command includes sacred and ordinary places and times, since the enemy persecuted Muslims even at the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: وأطلق الوجدان فشمل الحل والحرم من الزمان والمكان لأنهم كذلك يفعلون بالمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The action wording hints that God's party will prevail and the enemy cannot sustain resistance; experience shows fugitives do not return to fight.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بالفعل ما يشعر بالنصر بحزب الله وبشرى بضعف العدو عن مداومة المقاومة للمجاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to expel refers to Mecca, the home of pilgrimage, minor pilgrimage, and Islamic rites, as retribution for the believers' expulsion.
rows.anchor: أي مكة التي هي موطن الحج والعمرة ومحل الشعائر المقصودة لأهل الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here fitna means punishment through expulsion or other forms of intimidation.
rows.anchor: أي العذاب بالإخراج أو غيره من أنواع الإخافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persecution that turns people from Islam is worse than killing because it continually constricts the soul; combat is permitted as requital for expulsion, with expulsion itself the aim.
rows.anchor: أعم من أن يكون المراد من قتلكم إياهم في الحرم أو غيره أو قتلهم إياكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says ʿIkrima, Safwan ibn Umayya, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Rabiʿa embraced Islam when facing departure from Mecca as Islam prevailed, not from fear of being killed.
rows.anchor: وقد كشف الواقع في أمر : عكرمة بن أبي جهل وصفوان بن أمية وعبد الله بن أبي ربيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not fight at the sanctuary while expelling Quraysh unless they attack there; both location phrases mean the sanctuary, and combat should be avoided when possible out of reverence.
rows.anchor: أي الحرم إذا أردتم إخراجهم فمانعوكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording stresses restraint at the sanctuary, a place for prayer and prostration rather than fighting.
rows.anchor: والمراد الحرم في كل منهما كفا , عن القتال فيه مهما وجد إلى الكف سبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the enemy attacks in the sanctuary, believers may strike decisively rather than merely warding them off; the attacker bears responsibility for violating its sanctity.
rows.anchor: أي لا تقصروا على مدافعتهم بل اصدقوهم في الضرب المجهز ولا حرج عليكم

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read qatalūkum, while the majority has qātalūkum; either reading promises aid to the oppressed and their eventual victory.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بالفعل في جواب المفاعلة في قراءة الجمهور أو الفعل في قراءة حمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing phrase generalizes this consequence to all disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي مثل هذا الفعل العظيم الجدوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Desisting means stopping both fighting and its preliminaries.
rows.anchor: أي عن القتال ومقدماته , وفيه إشعار بأن طائفة منهم تنتهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has always been Forgiving and Merciful, and this is how He treats anyone who repents.
rows.anchor: أي له هاتان الصفتان أزلا وأبدا فكل من تاب فهذا شأنه معه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali reads the pilgrimage setting through resurrection: arrival at God's sanctuary in Paradise and Zamzam as a sign for Paradise's people completes the pilgrimage rulings.
rows.anchor: كذلك اعتباره موطنا إلى غاية الإفاضة والحلول بحرم الله في الآخرة التي هي الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the gathering is the fullest conclusion to the rules of pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: فلأجل ذلك كان أتم ختم لأحكام الحج ذكر الحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At this point the passage has completed its account of Islam's five foundations: faith, prayer, almsgiving, fasting, and pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وهنا تم ما أراد سبحانه وتعالى من بيان قواعد الإسلام الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith, prayer, and almsgiving were indicated at the sūra's beginning; pilgrimage is treated later for added emphasis after fasting.
rows.anchor: المشار إلى الثلاث الأول منها بقوله تعالى أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After discussing those seeking worldly benefit alone and those seeking both worlds, the passage notes the absent type rejecting both and the type seeking only the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ولما كان قد ذكر سبحانه وتعالى الراغب في الدنيا وحدها والراغب في الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dangerous case is a hypocrite who secretly seeks worldly gain while publicly presenting himself as seeking the afterlife.
rows.anchor: إنما هو المسر لإرادة الدنيا بإظهاره لإرادة الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placed after warnings of piety and resurrection, this portrait threatens the hypocrite with resurrection and recalls the hypocrites at the sūra's opening despite the long interval.
rows.anchor: بدأ به بعد ذكر التقوى والحشر ليكون مصدوعا بادئ بدء بذلك الأمر مقصودا بالتهديد بالحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min al-nās here means either a person or the person who has the described traits.
rows.anchor: أي شخص أو الذي { يعجبك } أي يروقك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuʿjibuka means that the person's speech pleases the listener and captures his heart; this echoes the hypocrite's deception at the sūra's beginning.
rows.anchor: كما ذكرنا أول السورة أنه يخادع , ويعجب من الإعجاب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines wonder as a thing's standing outside its peers, becoming rare in its kind of workmanship.
rows.anchor: قاله الحرالي . وقال الأصبهاني : حالة تغشى الإنسان

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani describes astonishment as a state covering someone who perceives excellence whose cause is unknown.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصبهاني : حالة تغشى الإنسان عند إدراك كمال مجهول السبب

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says astonishment depends on whether the observer knows the cause; the thing appears without a known cause to that observer.
rows.anchor: وعن الراغب أنه قال : وليس هو شيئا له في ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification limits impressive speech to worldly life; speech in the afterlife will not be good or admirable, avoiding confusion after the preceding mention of resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ذكر هذا بعد ذكر الحشر ربما أوهم

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls God as witness that his heart matches what he has displayed with his tongue.
rows.anchor: أنه مطابق لما أظهره بلسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He persists in false dispute without stopping, disguising his ugly purpose and making each argument seem attractive.
rows.anchor: أي يتمادى في الخصام بالباطل لا ينقطع جداله كل ذلك وهو يظهر أنه على الحسن الجميل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali glosses lidad as the opposite of disputation, and khisām as speech entering the hearer's ear to restrain a claim.
rows.anchor: واللدد ذدة الخصومة , والخصام القول الذي يسمع

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani defines khisām as excessive probing into a matter and constraining debate.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصبهاني : هو التعمق في البحث عن الشيء والمضايقة فيه

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani allows khisām itself to be described as aladd by way of hyperbole.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يجعل الخصام ألد على المبالغة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: The author suggests the differing order of fasting and pilgrimage in versions of Ibn ʿUmar's sound report about Islam's five foundations reflects this arrangement.
rows.anchor: حديث ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما في الصحيح ( بني الإسلام على خمس )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse explains how the hypocrite's contentiousness appears in action.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر أنه ألد شرع يذكر وجه لدده فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawalla can mean turning away inwardly or leaving the person he had deceived with his speech.
rows.anchor: أي أعرض بقلبه أو قاله عمن خدعه بكلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb saʿā depicts him hastening with full effort to stir discord.
rows.anchor: وكنى بالتعبير بالسعي عن الإسراع في إيقاع الفتنة بغاية الجهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasād is a name for all sins; his actions and words spread corruption throughout the land, especially among supporters.
rows.anchor: أي كلها بفعله وقوله عند من يوافقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His initial aim is to corrupt relations and enlist accomplices to bring destruction; destruction then enables further corruption.
rows.anchor: ونظمت الآية هكذا إفهاما لأن المعنى أن غرضه أولا بإفساد ذات البين التوصل إلى الإهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-harth means cultivated produce on which animals live; al-Harali says it is named for human cultivation, unlike planting attributed to God.
rows.anchor: أي المحروث الذي يعيش به الحيوان , قال الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harvest is a cause of animal life: destroying the cause destroys its effect, while the reverse is not necessarily true.
rows.anchor: ولأنه إذا هلك السبب هلك المسبب من غير عكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nasl means offspring, through which the animal kind continues.
rows.anchor: أي المنسول الذي به بقاء نوع الحيوان

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines nasl as the subtle part extracted from a whole.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو استخراج لطيف الشيء من جملته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God neither commands nor approves corruption; He forbids it, changes it, and punishes it even when punishment is delayed.
rows.anchor: لا يفعل فيه فعل المحب فلا يأمر به بل ينهى عنه ولا يقر عليه بل يغيره وإن طال المدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says corruption rather than destruction because destruction may be outward only and beneficial, as in requital.
rows.anchor: لأنه قد يكون صورة فقط فيكون صلاحا كما إذا كان قصاصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasād is chosen over ifsād because the latter can include corruption caused without intent.
rows.anchor: ولا قال : الإفساد يشمل ما إذا كان الفساد عن غير قصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses ihtibāk: corruption mentioned first implies its omission later, while destruction mentioned second implies its omission first.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك , ذكر أولا الإفساد ليدل على حذفه ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second ihtibāk pairs harvest as cause, implying offspring, and offspring as effect, implying crops.
rows.anchor: وذكر الحرث الذي هو السبب دلالة على الناسل والنسل الذي هو المسبب دلالة على الزرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His response to admonition distinguishes him from people who stop when corrected, confirming his extreme contentiousness.
rows.anchor: ولما كان من الناس من يفعل الفساد فإذا نهى عنه انتهى بين أن هذا على غير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone may warn him to leave corruption out of fear of God, under whose power everything lies.
rows.anchor: أي الملك الأعظم الذي كل شيء تحت قهره واترك ما أنت عليه من الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogance takes hold through ingrained pride and contempt for God's command; such pride is not proper to creatures.
rows.anchor: في نفسه لما فيها من الكبرياء والاستهانة بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True might belongs to God alone, as the author recalls with the phrase that all might belongs to God.
rows.anchor: وليس من شأن الخلق الاتصاف بذلك فإن العزة لله جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is seized by arrogance while sinning: base conduct that violates what is lawful and includes contempt and haughtiness toward others.
rows.anchor: أي مصاحبا للذنب , وهو العمل الرذل السافل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is punishment enough for him and becomes his bed, matching the way he prepared himself to pursue corruption.
rows.anchor: تكون مهادا له كما مهد للفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahannam suggests a grim face-to-face reception, fitting his confrontation of the person who admonished him.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص هذا الاسم المنبئ عن الجهامة في المواجهة أي الاستقبال بوجه كريه لما وقع منه من المواجهة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says God uses a particular name for the Fire when it conveys a meaning relevant to the judgment.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : فلمعنى ما يختص بالحكم يسمي تعالى النار باسم من أسمائها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines mihād as a place of rest or a comfortable, prepared thing that is spread and trodden.
rows.anchor: والمهاد موطن الهدوء والمستطاب مما يستفرش ويوطأ

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali sees the verse as respite for this community out of regard for its Prophet: evildoers and disbelievers face the afterlife, with a long stay and eternity there.
rows.anchor: فيه إشعار بإمهال الله عز وجل لهذه الأمة رعاية لنبيها فأحسب فاجرها وكافرها بعذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali adds that hastening worldly punishment for believers would leave disbelievers worldly life while believers receive the next life.
rows.anchor: ولو عاجل مؤمنها بعقوبة الدينا فخلص لكافرها الدنيا ولمؤمنها الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage contrasts the worst type, who destroys others to preserve himself, with the best, who risks himself to reform others.
rows.anchor: ولما أتم الخبر عن هذا القسم الذي هو شر الأقسام أتبعه خيرها ليكون ختاما وبينهما تباين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The self-sacrificing person gives himself up or purchases his own liberation through obedience, correcting the corrupt person and urging piety and remembrance.
rows.anchor: بالاجتهاد في أوامر الله بالنهي لمثل هذا الألد عن فعله الخبيث والأمر له بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is reported that the verse came down about Suhayb: when Quraysh tried to stop his emigration, he gave them his property and they let him go; the Prophet praised the sale. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وروي أنها نزلت في صهيب رضي الله تعالى عنه لأنه لما هاجر أرادت قريش رده فجعل لهم ماله حتى خلوا سبيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Suhayb report, shara means “purchased”; the Prophet called it a profitable sale.
rows.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( ربح البيع )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtighāʾ means seeking, easing, and facilitating the pursuit of God's pleasure; its mīmī verbal noun indicates time and place, and its extended ending marks its utmost degree.
rows.anchor: أي تطلب وتسهل وتيسر بغاية ما يمكن أن يكون كل من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mīmī verbal noun for divine pleasure indicates time and place, and its extended tāʾ signals culmination.
rows.anchor: بما دل عليه كون المصدر ميميا ويكون ذلك غاية في بابه بما دل عليه من وقفه بالتاء الممدودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is intensely compassionate toward all servants, blessing them outwardly and inwardly despite disbelief or shortcomings.
rows.anchor: أي بالغ الرحمة , وأظهر موضع الإضمار دلالة على العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God clarifies the path through reason, messengers, religious laws, and the books that preserve those laws.
rows.anchor: وبين لهم الطريق غاية البيان بالعقل أولا والرسل ثانيا والشرائع ثالثا والكتب الحافظة لها رابعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The numbered days separate the four human types because of their link to pilgrimage; their later placement signals they are not essential rites and can be compensated by an offering.
rows.anchor: ولعل الفصل بين الأقسام الأربعة بالأيام المعدودات اهتماما بأمرها لكونها من فعل الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to believers follows the self-sacrificing example so it lands immediately on the attentive listener, just as the hypocrite's portrait followed warnings of piety and resurrection.
rows.anchor: حسن جدا تعقيبه بقوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the call to faith among acts of worship strengthens its command and shows that faith is the foundation of guidance and salvation on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: وتكرير الأمر بالإيمان بين طوائف الأعمال من أعظم دليل علىحكمة الآمر به

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says addressing spouses directly encourages marriage matters to remain private, with waiting and resumption occurring under their bond rather than through judges.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفي مورد هذا الخطاب بإسناده للأزواج ما يظافر معنى إجراء أمور النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath of abstention does not become divorce merely when four months pass: the husband must resume relations or divorce, and if he refuses the judge divorces on his behalf.
rows.anchor: مبينا أن الطلاق لا يقع بمجرد مضي الأربعة الأشهر بل إما أن يفيء أو يطلق فإن أبى طلق عليه الحاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ʿazamū al-ṭalāq, divorce is the direct object of resolve without a preposition, signifying that they leave hesitation and decide plainly to execute it.
rows.anchor: فأوقع عليه العزم من غير حرف جر بمعنى أنهم تركوا ما كانوا فيه من الذبذبة وجعلوا الطلاق عزيمة واقعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm is firm resolve to carry out an act; al-Harali likens divorce to releasing something from one's hand that may later be taken back.
rows.anchor: والعزم الإجماع على إنفاذ الفعل , والطلاق هو في المعنى بمنزلة إطلاق الشيء من اليد الذي يمكن أخذه بعد إطلاقه - قاله الحرالي

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali takes God's hearing to indicate that divorce requires an outward verbal expression that can be heard.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : في إشارته إعلام بأن الطلاق لا بد له من ظاهر لفظ يقع مسموعا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: God's knowledge warns that spouses may privately harm or quarrel in matters beyond judges' reach, so they are entrusted with what is inward and outward.
rows.anchor: وفيه تهديد بما يقع في الأنفس والبواطن من المضارة والمضاجرة بين الأزواج في أمور لا تأخذها الأحكام

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars regard divorce as a trust in men's hands, just as counting the waiting period and establishing the womb's clearance are trusts in women's hands.
rows.anchor: ولذلك رأى العلماء أن الطلاق أمانة في أيدي الرجال كما أن العدد والاستبراء أمانة في أيدي النساء

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali links the wife's waiting after divorce to the husband's waiting during abstention, treating each as that spouse's trust.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : لما ذكر تربص الزوج - سبحانه وتعالى في أمر الطلاق الذي هو أمانته ذكر تربص المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third ruling, persisting in harm, is left unstated to signal that spouses should shun it; perpetrators face the opposite of mercy and forgiveness under the known legal ruling.
rows.anchor: وبقي من أحكام الإيلاء سم ثالث ترك التصريح به إشارة إلى أنهم ينبغي أن يكونوا في غاية النزاهة عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the divorced women are those whose marriages were consummated; pregnant women and those whose waiting periods are counted in months for young or old age are outside this discussion.
rows.anchor: أي المدخول بهن بما أفهمه الإيلاء من أن الكلام فيهن غير الحوامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declarative form, built on a subject and phrased as an accomplished fact, emphasizes the waiting duty and urges prompt compliance.
rows.anchor: في صيغة الخبر الذي من شأنه أن يكون قد وجد وانقضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatarabbaṣna means that divorced women wait and count out the prescribed period.
rows.anchor: أي ينتظرن اعتدادا . ولما كانت النفس داعية إلى الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase calls women to restrain themselves from seeking another husband or signaling availability through adornment, eye makeup, or suggestive speech before the waiting period ends.
rows.anchor: خص الأول معبرا لها بالنفس هزا إلى الاحتياط في كمال التربص والاستحياء مما يوهم الاستعجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting protects against eagerness to resume relations with another man before the prescribed period ends.
rows.anchor: فلا يطمعنها في مواصلة رجل قبل انقضاء العدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurūʾ can mean purity or menstruation, but the author prefers purity: the root concerns gathering, actual in purity; menstruation is named because it causes that gathering.
rows.anchor: وأن المراد بالقروء الأطهار لأنها زمن جمع الدم حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues that quruʾ, masculine in form with a feminine numeral, fits purity; the feminine noun menstruation takes a masculine numeral, supporting his preference.
rows.anchor: كان مذكرا يؤنث عدده

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani says purity is pluralized aqraʾ and qurūʾ, while menstruation is pluralized only aqraʾ; the forms therefore favor purity.
rows.anchor: والمشهور من كلام أهل اللغة أن جمع القرء بمعنى الطهر أقراء وقروء

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says qurūʾ is the boundary between purity and menstruation, attributable to either; this liminal meaning explains scholarly disagreement.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : قروء جمع قرء وهو الحد الفاصل بين الطهر والحيض

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali's sequence begins with divorce in a clean period without intercourse; each purity ending in bleeding completes a cycle, and the third bleed completes the waiting period.
rows.anchor: فإذا انتهى الطهر وابتدأ الحيض كان ما بينهما قرءا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: On al-Harali's account, the waiting period ends when the woman sees blood of the third menstruation, which accords with purity and is nearer than menstruation as the meaning of qurūʾ.
rows.anchor: فلذلك يعرب معناه عن حل المرأة عند رؤيتها الدم من الحيضة الثالثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Desire may lead women to conceal pregnancy to shorten the waiting period and attribute a child to a new husband, or to conceal menstruation out of desire for their former husband's return.
rows.anchor: وكان حبك للشيء يعمي ويصم وكان النساء أرغب في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God created in their wombs means either a child or menstrual blood.
rows.anchor: أي الذي له الأمر كله من ولد أو دم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines the womb as reproductive organs containing the fetus as it develops from a sperm drop into another form of creation.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو ما يشتمل على الولد من أعضاء التناسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not prove that pregnancy can be known with certainty; only its signs can be known.
rows.anchor: وليس فيه دليل على أن الحمل يعلم , إنما تعلم أماراته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although phrased as a report denying permissibility, the wording establishes prohibition and emphasizes it.
rows.anchor: ولما كان معنى هذا الإخبار النهي ليكون نافيا للحل بلفظه

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Concealing such matters indicates lack of faith in God and the Last Day, when God's greatness will be fully manifest and deeds repaid.
rows.anchor: الذي تظهر فيه عظمته أتم ظهور ويدين فيه العباد بما فعلوا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali takes the wording to imply a kind of hypocrisy in a woman who conceals what is in her womb; the author notes that this is a qualified attribution.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : ففي إشعاره إثبات نوع نفاق على الكاتمة ما في رحمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buʿūla means their husbands and is the plural of baʿl.
rows.anchor: أي أزواجهن , جمع بعل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines baʿl as a man prepared and able to marry a woman; it also means husband or master.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو الرجل المتهيئ لنكاح الأنثى المتأتي له ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A husband may restore the bond during the waiting period of a revocable divorce; after it ends, the woman has the stronger claim over herself.
rows.anchor: في أيام الأقراء فإذا انقضت صارت أحق بنفسها منه بها لانقضاء حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The husband's right of return is conditioned on intending reconciliation; without that intent, if she seeks separation, his act is inwardly adulterous.
rows.anchor: وهذا تنبيه على أنه إن لم يرد الإصلاح وأرادت هي السراح

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says repairing the first marriage is more fitting in God's wisdom than beginning another bond, because the past can trouble the present.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : الإصلاح لخلل ما بينهما أحق في علم الله وحكمته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Harali invokes the Prophet's warning against marrying al-lafoot, a woman who has a child from a previous husband; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: مما حذر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نكاح اللفوت وهي التي لها ولد من زوج سابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women have reciprocal rights in recognized good conduct, though the rights need not be identical in kind because each suits its holder's role.
rows.anchor: أي في كونه حسنة في نفسه على ما يليق بملك منهما لا في النوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples include the husband's return right balanced by her right to good companionship, and his ability to retain her balanced by her right to a companion who relieves loneliness.
rows.anchor: فكما للرجال الرجعة قهرا فلهن العشرة بالجميل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines maʿrūf as what the law approves, reason accepts, and noble character welcomes.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : والمعروف ما أقره الشرع وقبله العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Men have a degree over women, including but not limited to husbands, in such matters as maintenance and the bridal payment.
rows.anchor: أي فضل من جهات لا يخفى كالإنفاق والمهر

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali attributes the degree to men's greater steadiness of intellect and completeness of religion.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : لما أوثروا به من رصانة العقل وتمام الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author quantifies the difference as one degree in three, citing the equivalence of two women to one man.
rows.anchor: فالرجل يزيد على المرأة بدرجة من ثلاث لأن كل امرأتين بمنزلة رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone has true might; any might He lends others is His power's garment, so all should fear His force.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه أعز بل لا عزيز إلا هو ليخشى كل من أعاره ثوب عزة سطوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's wisdom explains the arrangement and reassures women that what He establishes through might and perfects through wisdom cannot be undone.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على أنه ما فعل ذلك إلا لحكمة بالغة تسلية للنساء وإن ما أوجده بعزته وأتقنه بحكمته لا يمكن نقضه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The passage answers whether a husband could return and divorce a wife indefinitely during her waiting period, as men did before Islam.
rows.anchor: فكانت الآية كالمجمل عرض سؤال : هل هي ممتدة كما كانوا يفعلون في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says revocable divorce is limited to two occasions on which the marriage can be repaired by return.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : لما كان الطلاق لما يتهيأ رده قصره الحق تعالى على المرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says “two times” rather than “two divorces” to encourage separating the acts, one at a time instead of combining them.
rows.anchor: دون طلقتان تنبيها - على أنه ينبغي أن تكون مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a second divorce during the waiting period, the husband may return or divorce; return is treated first as the more urgent issue, with the other case addressed after the waiting period.
rows.anchor: ولما كان له بعد الثانية في العدة حالان إعمال وإهمال وكان الإعمال إما بالرجعة وإما بالطلاق
